Command: Hold Fast and Be Faithful unto Death
Summary: The risen Christ's command in the Revelation letters: hold fast what you have, be faithful unto death, and receive the crown of life.
Commandment: Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. Hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.
Application: Spoken to Smyrna, Thyatira, and Philadelphia under pressure, merged here as one command because the wording and the charge are the same: endurance that does not let go under persecution.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'that no man take thy crown' (Revelation 3:11).
Function: Hold fast what you have, that no man take thy crown. Not Mosaic law but a New Testament command — the threefold division does not sort it. Its goal was endurance under pressure — spoken to Smyrna, Thyatira, and Philadelphia, and merged here because the wording and the charge are the same. The evil it addressed was letting go under persecution, trading faithfulness for ease. It restrained that evil by the promise joined to it: be faithful unto death, and receive the crown of life.
